questions.q:
The correct statements among I to III are:
(I) Valence bond theory cannot explain the color exhibited by transition metal complexes.
(II) Valence bond theory can predict quantitatively the magnetic properties of transition metal complexes.
(III) Valence bond theory cannot distinguish ligands as weak and strong field ones.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Valence Bond Theory (VBT) has several limitations in explaining the properties of coordination compounds.

Statement (I) is correct. VBT does not explain the optical properties or the color exhibited by transition metal complexes. The color is primarily due to d-d electron transitions, which are successfully explained by Crystal Field Theory (CFT).

Statement (II) is incorrect. VBT only provides a qualitative idea about the magnetic properties, such as whether a complex is paramagnetic or diamagnetic based on the presence of unpaired electrons. It cannot predict magnetic properties quantitatively.

Statement (III) is correct. VBT does not distinguish between weak field and strong field ligands. It relies on experimentally observed magnetic moments to assume whether inner or outer d-orbitals are used for hybridization, without explaining why certain ligands cause electron pairing while others do not. The classification of ligands into weak and strong fields is a feature of CFT.

Therefore, only statements (I) and (III) are correct.

questions.q:
If Ni2+ is replaced by Pt2+ in the complex NiCl2Br22-, which of the following properties are expected to get changed?
A. Geometry
B. Geometrical isomerism
C. Optical isomerism
D. Magnetic properties
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
When Ni2+ is replaced by Pt2+ in the complex NiCl2Br22-, the following properties are expected to be changed:

A. Geometry: Since Pt2+ and Ni2+ have different coordination preferences and atomic sizes, the replacement is likely to result in a change in the geometry of the complex. That is it changes to square planar.

B. Geometrical isomerism: If the replacement of Ni2+ with Pt2+ leads to a change in the ligand arrangement, it can result in the generation of cis and trans isomers.

C. Magnetic properties: PtCl2Br22- is diamagnetic.

Both the complex species are optically inactive.

If the CFSE of TiH2O63+ is -96.0 kJ/mol, this complex will absorb maximum at wavelength nm. (nearest integer)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
In TiH2O63+, oxidation state of Titanium is +3.
Thus, electronic configuration:

Ti+3:3d1⇒t2g1,0,0,eg0,0

We know CFSE =-0.4nt2g+0.6negΔo       (    Δo = Octahedral splitting energy)

Δo=96×1030.4×6×1023=4×10-19 J

Using planck's equation and fact that octahedral splitting energy per complex is:
⇒Δo=hcλ=4×10-19 J

⇒λ=6.4×10-34×3×1084×10-19=4.8×10-7 m

⇒λ=480×10-9 m

∴λ=480 nm

Number of complexes which show optical isomerism among the following is _________.

cis-Cr(ox)2Cl23-,Co(en)33+, cis -Pt(en)2Cl22+, cis -Co(en)2Cl2+

​​​​​​​,trans-Pt(en)2Cl22+, trans -Cr(ox)2Cl23-
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Pt(en)2Cl22+ is a square planar complex forms geometrical isomers (cis and trans). Trans isomer does not show optical isomerism since it is symmetrical, while cis isomer shows optical isomerism as it is unsymmetrical.

POS = plane of symmetry

COS = centre of symmetry

The compounds,  cis−[Co(en)2Cl2]+ and [Co(en)3]3+ show optical isomerism as they do not possess any element of symmetry.

cis-Cr(ox)2Cl23-→can show optical isomerism (no POS & COS)

trans-Pt(en)2Cl22+→can't show optical isomerism (contain POS & COS)
